seoTitle: Histogram Builder with Bin Width Control (SVG)
metaDescription: Bin a list of numbers into a histogram with your own bin width or an automatic one. Free, shows counts per bin, exports SVG.
intro: Counts how many of your numbers fall in each bin and draws the bars. You set the bin width and where the first bin starts.
why:
The shape of a histogram changes with the bin width, so being able to change it is the whole point. Try several widths and watch whether a second peak appears or disappears.

Bins include their lower edge and exclude the upper edge; the last bin includes both. The table under the chart lists every bin and count, so you can copy the numbers. Automatic width picks a round number from the Sturges rule, which suits roughly bell-shaped data and can hide detail in skewed data.
howTo: Paste numbers separated by spaces, commas or new lines.
Set a bin width, or 0 for automatic, and optionally the first bin start.
Compare the picture with different widths.
Copy the SVG or the counts table.

faq.q: Which edge belongs to which bin?
faq.a: A value equal to a bin edge goes into the bin that starts there. Only the last bin also includes its upper edge.

faq.q: How many numbers can it take?
Can I use percentages instead of counts?
faq.a: Not yet. The y axis shows counts.
Bin counts for the sample were checked against a manual Python count.
